description_good_justification: The website and README say what it is: the open source launcher for macOS, with one hotkey to search apps, commands, quicklinks and System Settings panes, and it runs Raycast extensions unmodified. https://www.getthaw.app/floe
interact_justification: The website and README link to the download, the repository has issue templates for bugs and feature requests, and the README links to the contributing guide. https://www.getthaw.app/floe https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/issues/new/choose https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe#contributing
contribution_justification: Contributions go through forks and pull requests against the development branch, with issues for discussion: https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: The guide sets the requirements: Conventional Commit titles, the pull request template, DCO sign-off, tests and passing checks: https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md Coding standards: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/CODING_STANDARDS.md
floss_license_justification: Released under AGPL-3.0: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/LICENSE Ported code keeps its own FLOSS terms: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/LICENSES/README.md
floss_license_osi_justification: AGPL-3.0 is approved by the Open Source Initiative.
documentation_basics_justification: The website documents installing, starting and using Floe, and warns that extensions are not sandboxed, so install only ones you trust: https://www.getthaw.app/floe The security policy covers the same limit: https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md
documentation_interface_justification: Floe's external interface is the Raycast extension API, documented by Raycast. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/COMPAT.md lists what Floe does with each part of it, and https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/LIMITATIONS.md lists the gaps.
sites_https_justification: The website, repository and downloads use HTTPS, and the website redirects HTTP to HTTPS. https://www.getthaw.app/floe https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/releases
discussion_justification: GitHub issues, pull requests and discussions are searchable, addressable by URL, open to new people and need no proprietary client software: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/issues
english_justification: Documentation is in English, and bug reports and code comments are accepted in English. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe#readme
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: four releases in October 2026, the latest 0.2.1. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/releases
repo_track_justification: Git records each change, its author and its date: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/commits/development
repo_interim_justification: Development happens in public on branches and pull requests between releases: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/pulls
version_unique_justification: Each release has its own version number, such as 0.2.1: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/releases
version_semver_justification: Versions use the Semantic Versioning format, such as 0.2.1 or 0.2.0-beta.1.
version_tags_justification: Each release has a Git tag: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/tags
release_notes_justification: Each release has its own notes in the changelog, written for users and not taken from the Git log. The GitHub Release and the update feed use them: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability with a CVE or similar has been fixed in Floe. Fixes from security scans are still listed under Security in the changelog: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/CHANGELOG.md
report_process_justification: Users report bugs with the issue template: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/issues/new/choose
report_responses_justification: The project's first reports date from October 2026. Of 4 bug reports not withdrawn by their author, the maintainer answered or closed 3 (#3, #18, #39). https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/issues
enhancement_responses_justification: The maintainer answered or completed 3 of the 5 requests from other people (#40, #42, #46). https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/issues
report_archive_justification: All issues stay public and searchable: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The process is in the security policy: https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Reporters use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting, which is enabled and runs over HTTPS: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: Floe received no vulnerability reports in the last 6 months.
build_justification: Floe builds with xcodebuild from the generated Xcode project, or with SwiftPM (swift build). The Rust index builds with Cargo. Steps: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md
build_common_tools_justification: Uses SwiftPM, xcodebuild, XcodeGen, Cargo and Bun.
build_floss_tools_justification: Floe is a native macOS app. Building it needs Apple's macOS SDK and Xcode, which are proprietary and have no FLOSS replacement for AppKit and SwiftUI. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#run
test_justification: The test suites are in the repository under the project's AGPL-3.0 license: Swift Testing in Tests/FloeTests, bun test in runtime/tests, cargo test for the Rust index, and Python unittest in scripts/tests.
test_invocation_justification: Uses each language's standard command: swift test, bun --config=runtime/bunfig.toml test ./runtime, cargo test, and python3 -m unittest. Listed in https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md
test_most_justification: The latest CI run reports 86.5% line coverage (23719/27410). That figure leaves out code that can't run in a unit test, such as views and system calls, listed with reasons in https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/sonar-project.properties
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions builds and runs all test suites on every pull request and push to development that changes code:https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/actions/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: The contribution guidelines say: "Add automated tests for new behavior and regression tests for bug fixes when practical." https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md The coding standards also require 80% coverage on new code: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/CODING_STANDARDS.md
tests_are_added_justification: Recent major changes added or updated tests. For example, https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/pull/34 touched 28 test files, https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/pull/36 touched 9 and https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/pull/47 touched 8.
tests_documented_added_justification: Test expectations are in the contribution guidelines: https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings_justification: Uses Swift 6 language mode with complete concurrency checking, SwiftLint, and SonarCloud and CodeQL analysis.
warnings_fixed_justification: The latest CI build had no compiler warnings in project code, and swiftlint --strict fails CI on any new lint warning. Existing size and complexity violations (19) are recorded in .swiftlint.baseline.
warnings_strict_justification: Uses Swift 6 strict concurrency and swiftlint --strict. Compiler warnings do not fail the build, and Tests and Vendor are not linted.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer knows these principles and applies them, for example fail-safe checks on messages between Floe's processes, which are authenticated with HMAC, and secrets held in the Keychain. Security fixes are listed in the changelog: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/CHANGELOG.md
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common errors for a desktop app that runs extensions and how to counter them, such as injection (AppleScript values are escaped) and missing authorization (an extension's tokens go only to the folder that saved them). https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/pull/53
crypto_published_justification: Uses only published algorithms: SHA-256, HMAC-SHA-256 and TLS, and Ed25519 signatures for updates through Sparkle.
crypto_call_justification: Calls Apple's CryptoKit and system TLS, Web Crypto in the runtime, and Sparkle for update signatures. Floe implements no cryptography of its own.
crypto_floss_justification: Everything that depends on cryptography uses open standards that FLOSS can implement, such as SHA-256, HMAC, TLS and Ed25519.
crypto_keylength_justification: Uses 256-bit HMAC keys, SHA-256 and Ed25519. No setting offers shorter lengths.
crypto_working_justification: Uses no broken algorithms or inappropriate cipher modes. The code has no MD5 or SHA-1.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Does not use SHA-1, CBC in SSH or other algorithms with known serious weaknesses.
crypto_pfs_justification: Floe implements no key agreement protocol. Its HTTPS goes through Apple's networking, with App Transport Security on except for local network addresses.
crypto_password_storage_justification: Floe does not authenticate external users with passwords. Secrets for other services are kept in the macOS Keychain.
crypto_random_justification: Keys come from CryptoKit's SymmetricKey, and OAuth values from Web Crypto's getRandomValues and randomUUID. These are cryptographically secure generators.
delivery_mitm_justification: Downloads and updates use HTTPS. The app is signed and notarized, and Sparkle checks update signatures with Ed25519. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/releases
delivery_unsigned_justification: Releases publish checksums over HTTPS with Sigstore signatures, and Sparkle checks an Ed25519 signature on each update.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No published advisories or CVEs, and no open Dependabot alerts. Dependency findings must be resolved before merge: https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been reported. Findings from the security scan of 0.2.0 were fixed and released the next day as 0.2.1: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/pull/53
no_leaked_credentials_justification: GitHub secret scanning and push protection are on, with no open alerts. No key or certificate files are tracked in Git, and signing secrets are kept in a protected GitHub environment.
static_analysis_justification: SwiftLint and SonarCloud run on pull requests that change code, CodeQL runs on JavaScript/TypeScript and Actions weekly, and CodeRabbit security scans ran on 0.1.0 and 0.2.0. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/ci.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL, SonarCloud and CodeRabbit's security scan all look for common vulnerabilities.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: The maintainer fixes and releases confirmed findings, such as the CodeQL alerts in https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/pull/38 and the scan findings in https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/pull/53. No CodeQL alerts are open.
static_analysis_often_justification: SwiftLint and SonarCloud run on pull requests that change code, except that SonarCloud skips forks and Dependabot. CodeQL also runs weekly. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: libFuzzer with AddressSanitizer runs in CI nightly and on any change to IncomingLink.swift, the code that reads links from other apps, or to its harness. A release does not wait for a run. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Floe is written in Swift, Rust and TypeScript, which are memory-safe, with no C, C++ or Objective-C source of its own. A small amount of Swift and Rust uses unsafe code at system boundaries.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzz harness checks its properties with precondition calls, which stay on in its build, under AddressSanitizer. Unit tests run in debug builds, which keep Swift's runtime safety checks on. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/Fuzzing/Sources/FuzzIncomingLink/FuzzIncomingLink.swift
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Dynamic analysis has found no vulnerabilities.
access_continuity_justification: The other organization owners keep admin access to the repository and can start a release: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
assurance_case_justification: The assurance case covers the threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles, common weaknesses and residual risks: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
signed_releases_justification: Releases are notarized and signed with a Developer ID, Sparkle EdDSA and Sigstore, and users can check each one: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/VERIFYING_RELEASES.md
bus_factor_justification: Thaw's governance applies to Floe, so its three organization owners (stonerl, nightah, diazdesandi) share continuity for the project: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
contributors_unassociated_justification: Outside contributors with no tie to each other wrote significant features: OwenCope the built-in search, extension APIs and store (#6), lylythechosenone the calculator (#7), and unsecretised the Quit command and store settings (#16, #19). https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/graphs/contributors
code_review_standards_justification: The governance document says who reviews, what a reviewer checks and which changes get a security read: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
small_tasks_justification: Issue 1 lists tasks for newcomers under the good first issue label: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/issues/1
security_review_justification: The assurance case reviews the design against the security requirements and trust boundaries, and CodeRabbit's security scans of 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 led to fixes in #45 and #53: https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The thaw-app organization requires two-factor authentication for every member. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md
osps_ac_02_01_justification: The organization's base permission is read, and owners grant write access by hand. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md
osps_ac_03_01_justification: Branch protection on development requires a pull request, so a direct push is refused. Organization owners can bypass it. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
osps_ac_03_02_justification: Branch protection and a ruleset with no bypass block deleting development. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The repository and organization default the workflow token to read, and each workflow declares read-only top-level permissions. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/ci.yml
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Jobs that need more ask for it themselves, such as id-token for signing or pull-requests for PR Metadata. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/release.yml https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/pr-metadata.yml
osps_br_01_01_justification: PR Metadata runs on pull_request_target and never checks out the pull request's code. No workflow puts a pull request's title, body or branch name in a shell script. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/pr-metadata.yml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Fork pull requests get no secrets and Sonar is skipped for them. The .build command refuses a fork's branch, and signing secrets stay in the prod Environment behind approval. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/ci.yml https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#releases-and-secrets
osps_br_01_04_justification: Collaborator inputs reach scripts through environment variables, and release.yml rejects a tag that isn't a version number or doesn't match the app's version. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/release.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: Each release has its own version tag. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/releases
osps_br_02_02_justification: Every asset is attached to its tag's GitHub Release. The SBOM and the update ZIP also carry the version in their names, and the DMG keeps the stable name Floe.dmg. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/releases
osps_br_03_01_justification: The repository, website, documentation and Discord invite are all HTTPS links. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/README.md
osps_br_03_02_justification: Releases come from GitHub over HTTPS, and Sparkle updates also check an EdDSA signature. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/VERIFYING_RELEASES.md
osps_br_04_01_justification: CHANGELOG.md records each release's changes, with a Security group for security fixes, and each GitHub Release carries notes. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/CHANGELOG.md https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/releases
osps_br_05_01_justification: Builds get dependencies with Swift Package Manager, Bun and Cargo from their lockfiles. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#dependencies
osps_br_06_01_justification: The app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized, the DMG and SBOM are signed with Sigstore, and updates are signed with EdDSA. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/VERIFYING_RELEASES.md
osps_br_07_01_justification: Signing material lives only in GitHub Actions secrets, and secret scanning with push protection is on. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#releases-and-secrets
osps_br_07_02_justification: Floe's governance says where release secrets live and who can use them, and Thaw's adds storage, rotation and owner agreement. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#releases-and-secrets https://github.com/thaw-app/Thaw/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#release-secrets
osps_do_01_01_justification: The README and the website's documentation cover installing and using Floe. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/README.md https://www.getthaw.app/docs/floe
osps_do_02_01_justification: The contribution guidelines and issue templates explain how to report a defect. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/issues/new/choose
osps_do_03_01_justification: Verifying releases explains how to check the signature, notarization, checksum, Sigstore bundle, provenance and Sparkle updates. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/VERIFYING_RELEASES.md
osps_do_03_02_justification: Verifying releases gives the expected Apple team ID and Sigstore identity. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/VERIFYING_RELEASES.md
osps_do_04_01_justification: Security fixes target the latest stable release, and alpha and beta releases get best-effort support. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_do_05_01_justification: Older releases are not supported, so a release stops getting security updates when a newer stable one ships. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_do_06_01_justification: DEVELOPMENT.md documents how dependencies are chosen, declared, locked, obtained and scanned. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#dependencies
osps_do_07_01_justification: DEVELOPMENT.md lists what you need and how to build and run Floe. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#run
osps_gv_01_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md names the maintainer and organization owners, and gives the access of write collaborators. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
osps_gv_01_02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md describes each role and its responsibilities. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
osps_gv_02_01_justification: Changes and problems are discussed publicly in GitHub issues and pull requests and on Discord. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#community-channels
osps_gv_03_01_justification: The shared contribution guidelines describe the process. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: The contribution guidelines set requirements for titles, tests, sign-off and AI-assisted work, and governance has a review checklist. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
osps_gv_04_01_justification: Thaw's governance applies to Floe: existing owners grant write and owner access, and access to secrets needs every owner's agreement. https://github.com/thaw-app/Thaw/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md
osps_le_01_01_justification: The Developer Certificate of Origin is required, and PR Metadata fails a commit with no matching Signed-off-by. Named bots are exempt. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/pr-metadata.yml
osps_le_02_01_justification: The source is licensed under AGPL-3.0, which is OSI approved and FSF free. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/LICENSE
osps_le_02_02_justification: Released software is under the same AGPL-3.0 terms. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/LICENSE
osps_le_03_01_justification: The license is in the LICENSE file, and third-party licenses are in LICENSES. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/LICENSE https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/LICENSES/README.md
osps_le_03_02_justification: The LICENSE file is in the repository each release is tagged from. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_01_justification: The repository is public at a static URL. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git history on GitHub publicly records each change, its author and its time. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/commits/development
osps_qa_02_01_justification: Direct dependencies are listed in Package.swift, runtime/package.json and Cargo.toml, with lockfiles beside them. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#dependencies
osps_qa_02_02_justification: Each release includes a CycloneDX SBOM with its checksum, Sigstore bundle and provenance. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/releases/tag/0.2.1
osps_qa_03_01_justification: Branch protection on development requires lint, build, sonarqube and dependency-sca to pass. Organization owners can bypass it. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
osps_qa_04_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md lists the repositories Floe's code and releases depend on. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#repository
osps_qa_04_02_justification: org-ci, the one other repository that builds releases, requires pull requests, status checks, signed commits and linear history on its main branch, with the same owners. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#repository
osps_qa_05_01_justification: The repository holds no generated executables. Binaries are published to GitHub Releases. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/releases
osps_qa_05_02_justification: The only binary files in the repository are two PNG images. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe
osps_qa_06_01_justification: CI runs the Swift and runtime test suites on every pull request that changes code. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/ci.yml
osps_qa_06_02_justification: DEVELOPMENT.md says what CI runs and when, and how to run the tests locally. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#tests
osps_qa_06_03_justification: The contribution guidelines ask for tests on new behavior and regression tests for bug fixes, and governance has reviewers check for them. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
osps_qa_07_01_justification: Branch protection on development requires an approval from someone other than the last pusher. Organization owners can bypass it. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
osps_sa_01_01_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md describes the processes and components, and the assurance case gives the actors and trust boundaries. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#trust-boundaries
osps_sa_02_01_justification: External interfaces lists what a release accepts and reaches out to. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/INTERFACES.md
osps_sa_03_01_justification: The assurance case records the most likely and most damaging problems, and the risks that remain. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_sa_03_02_justification: The assurance case has the threat model and attack surface, and governance requires updating it when a trust boundary moves. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#threat-model https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
osps_vm_01_01_justification: The Security Policy describes coordinated disclosure and aims to acknowledge reports within 48 hours. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#coordinated-disclosure
osps_vm_02_01_justification: The Security Policy gives the security contacts and the reporting path. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_03_01_justification: Private vulnerability reporting is on for the repository. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/security/advisories/new
osps_vm_04_01_justification: The policy publishes confirmed vulnerabilities as GitHub Security Advisories, and CHANGELOG.md has a Security group for each release's fixes. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#coordinated-disclosure https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/CHANGELOG.md
osps_vm_05_01_justification: The policy requires resolving every unsuppressed dependency finding whatever its severity, and a suppression needs a reason and an expiry. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#dependency-findings
osps_vm_05_02_justification: Findings are resolved before merge, so they are resolved before a release too. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#dependency-findings
osps_vm_05_03_justification: dependency-sca scans every pull request and is required on development. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/dependency-sca.yml https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
osps_vm_06_01_justification: DEVELOPMENT.md sets the limits for SonarCloud and CodeQL findings and how a finding is handled. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#security-findings
osps_vm_06_02_justification: The required sonarqube job waits for SonarCloud's quality gate and fails when the gate does. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/sonar-project.properties https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
osps_vm_04_02_justification: No dependency vulnerability has been found that doesn't affect Floe: osv-scanner.toml has no suppressions, so there is nothing for a VEX document to cover. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/osv-scanner.toml
achieve_passing_justification: Floe answers every passing criterion in this file. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.bestpractices.json
dco_justification: Contributors sign off under the Developer Certificate of Origin, and PR Metadata checks it. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md describes how decisions are made. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#decision-model
code_of_conduct_justification: Floe follows the organization's Code of Conduct. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md lists each role, who holds it and what it does. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
documentation_roadmap_justification: The roadmap lists what is up next, what comes later and what is not planned. Its items have no dates. https://www.getthaw.app/floe/roadmap
documentation_architecture_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md describes the processes and where the code lives. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
documentation_security_justification: The assurance case says what you can and can't expect from Floe's security. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#security-requirements
documentation_quick_start_justification: The README explains how to download and install Floe, and the website documents how to use it. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/README.md https://www.getthaw.app/docs/floe
documentation_current_justification: The contribution guidelines ask for documentation updates with each change, and reviewers check that the documentation matches. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
documentation_achievements_justification: The README links to the OpenSSF badges and the SLSA attestations. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/README.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: Floe uses AppKit and SwiftUI controls. 26 source files set accessibility labels or elements, and 6 follow Reduce Motion. It has had no formal accessibility audit.
internationalization_justification: Text the app shows goes through a String Catalog, and translations arrive through Crowdin. Only English has shipped so far. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#localization
maintenance_or_update_justification: Sparkle updates Floe from inside the app, and the Security Policy supports the latest stable release. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No outside reporter has filed a vulnerability. The changelog credits CodeRabbit's security scans for the fixes they led to, and the policy credits reporters. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/CHANGELOG.md https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#coordinated-disclosure
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: The Security Policy gives the process for reporting, acknowledging, fixing and disclosing a vulnerability. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md#coordinated-disclosure
coding_standards_justification: CODING_STANDARDS.md has the rules, and .swiftlint.yml and .swiftformat hold the tool settings. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/CODING_STANDARDS.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: CI runs SwiftLint in strict mode as lint, a required check on development. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/ci.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: xcodebuild and swift build add flags from the command line, such as OTHER_SWIFT_FLAGS and -Xswiftc. project.yml sets no such flags, and build-rust.sh leaves Cargo's RUSTFLAGS alone. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/project.yml
build_preserve_debug_justification: Release builds keep debug information in dSYM bundles, and nothing strips it at install. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#releases-and-updates
build_non_recursive_justification: Xcode and Swift Package Manager build from one dependency graph, with no recursive make. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/project.yml
build_repeatable_justification: Two clean unsigned Release builds for Apple silicon at the same path matched on 151 of the app's 152 files, including the Floe binary; Assets.car differed. Signed and notarized releases are not bit-identical. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#releases-and-updates
installation_common_justification: Floe installs the usual macOS way: open the disk image and drag it to Applications. Dragging it to the Trash removes it. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/README.md
installation_development_quick_justifica: Three commands install the runtime's packages, build the Rust index and open the project in Xcode, which also runs the tests. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#run
external_dependencies_justification: DEVELOPMENT.md lists each kind of dependency and where it is declared and locked. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#dependencies
dependency_monitoring_justification: dependency-sca scans the lockfiles with OSV-Scanner on every pull request and weekly, and Dependabot updates GitHub Actions and opens security updates. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/dependency-sca.yml https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/dependabot.yml
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Lockfiles identify each package and its version. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#dependencies
interfaces_current_justification: Two clean Release builds with Xcode 27 reported no deprecation warnings, and CI treats SwiftLint warnings as failures. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/ci.yml
automated_integration_testing_justificat: ci.yml runs the test suites on every pull request and on pushes to development and main, and reports the result as checks. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/.github/workflows/ci.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: 33 of the 44 fix commits on development in the last six months changed tests, which is 75%. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/commits/development
test_statement_coverage80_justification: SonarCloud reports 86.0% line coverage on development. Code that can't run in a unit test is excluded, and sonar-project.properties states the rule. https://sonarcloud.io/project/overview?id=thaw-app_Floe
test_policy_mandated_justification: The contribution guidelines ask for automated tests for new behavior, and the coding standards ask for a regression test for each bug fix. https://github.com/thaw-app/.github/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/CODING_STANDARDS.md#tests
implement_secure_design_justification: The assurance case shows how Floe applies each of Saltzer and Schroeder's principles. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#secure-design-principles
crypto_credential_agility_justification: AI keys and sign-in tokens are kept in the Keychain, apart from settings, and you can replace them in Floe without recompiling. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#security-requirements
crypto_used_network_justification: Floe's connections use HTTPS. App Transport Security allows plain HTTP only to local addresses, for local model servers. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/INTERFACES.md#network
crypto_tls12_justification: Floe uses URLSession, whose default minimum on the supported macOS versions is TLS 1.2, and doesn't lower it. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/INTERFACES.md#network
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Floe uses URLSession's default certificate verification, and neither the app nor the runtime overrides it. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: The system verifies the certificate before URLSession sends any request headers, and Floe doesn't override that. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe
input_validation_justification: IncomingLink accepts only known link schemes and hosts, and is fuzzed. Requests from extensions are parsed into known cases, and manifests and AI addresses are checked before use. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#trust-boundaries
hardening_justification: Releases use the hardened runtime and are notarized, and the app has no JIT or library validation exceptions. Swift and Rust add memory safety. Bun needs looser entitlements, which the assurance case records. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#residual-risks
sites_password_security_justification: GitHub hosts the repository and downloads, and the website has no accounts. Floe's sites store no passwords.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Floe installs by dragging an app to Applications, which has no convention like DESTDIR.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: Floe offers no choice of algorithm. macOS negotiates TLS, and Sparkle's EdDSA and the HMAC-SHA256 on messages between Floe's processes are fixed, so an update would replace them.
version_tags_signed_justification: Tags through 0.2.1 are not signed. The release steps now use git tag -s, so signing starts with the next tag. https://github.com/thaw-app/Floe/blob/development/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#releases-and-updates
